organization.name: Walnut (implementation), with Argot Collective (backer and format steward)
organization.summary: Walnut builds developer tooling including debuggers and implements ethdebug in solc under this grant. Its site says it partners with Argot Collective and the Ethereum Foundation on this work. Argot is a non-profit that maintains solc and Fe and stewards the ethdebug format, and the proposal says it committed up to 151,000 USD of the 279,000 USD budget.

previousFunding.label: Argot Collective funding of the first three milestones, as stated in the proposal (no Argot report found)
Ethereum Foundation described as trusting Walnut with core infrastructure, per Walnut's homepage

delivery.grant: Argot-funded milestone 1: testing and validation infrastructure (13,000 USD)
delivery.promised: Automated test and validation infrastructure for ethdebug output running in public CI. A merged pull request with a matching title exists in the solc repository, but no public source found links its author to Walnut, and the acceptance wording was not reviewed. The pull request is shown as unmatched to the grantee.

delivery.grant: Argot-funded milestone 2: internal debug data specification (19,000 USD)
delivery.promised: Internal specification of how solc represents and propagates debug data, published for review. A merged pull request with a matching title exists in the solc repository, but no public source found links its author to Walnut, and the acceptance wording was not reviewed. The pull request is shown as unmatched to the grantee.

delivery.grant: Argot-funded milestone 3: Yul serialization (33,000 USD, due 2026-10)
delivery.promised: Debug info survives compilation round-trips through Yul, shown by automated tests in public CI. Two open pull requests on this topic exist, but no public source found links their author to Walnut.

claims.claim: The first milestone (test infrastructure) is complete, linked to pull request 16727.
claims.method: GitHub API shows the pull request titled 'ethdebug: Improve current testing infra' is merged (2026-05-28). Whether the CI meets the acceptance wording was not reviewed. No public source found linking the author to Walnut.

claims.claim: The second milestone (internal debug data specification) is complete, linked to pull request 16780.
claims.method: GitHub API shows the pull request titled 'feat: add internal spec for debug-info' is merged (2026-08-19). The specification text was not reviewed. No public source found linking the author to Walnut.

claims.claim: The ethdebug format is an open specification with a public repository, comparable in intent to DWARF.
claims.method: The site resolves and the repository is active (last push 2026-11-24, 81 stars, 12 forks, no tagged release). The README states the DWARF comparison. The site marks the specification as Draft.

claims.claim: The implementation is underway at Walnut and lands in the official solc repository.

sources.label: Open ethdebug pull requests in solidity

claims.method: GitHub search shows over a dozen open ethdebug pull requests in argotorg/solidity opened 2026-11-23 to 2026-11-27, plus merged 16727 and 16780. No public source found linking the pull request authors (for example djolertrk, author of 16727 and 16780) to Walnut. Private organization membership cannot be seen, so this is a gap in public evidence only.

claims.claim: Walnut is building soldb, the first ETHDebug consumer, a CLI debugger and tracer for Solidity.
claims.method: The repository exists (GPL-3.0, 34 stars, last push 2026-11-26). The ethdebug site says debuggers such as Walnut's soldb read the format. Debugging output quality was not tested.

claims.claim: solc emits ethdebug data for the full unoptimized pipeline and then optimized builds, and soldb debugs optimized builds without source maps.
claims.method: These are open milestones due 2027-03 and 2027-06. The ethdebug site calls solc support experimental and local variables and optimized code upcoming.

claims.claim: At least 3 of 5 providers (Tenderly, Foundry, Hardhat, Medusa, Remix) will engage on adoption.
claims.method: This is a future adoption milestone. No written provider engagement was found.

claims.claim: The 2025 Solidity Developer Survey had 925 responses and ranked step-through debugging, variable inspection and transaction replay highest.
claims.method: Walnut's post repeats the figures. The survey report itself was not located in this check.
